sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F168].
Revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 to $13.7 billion, then rose 153.2% in FY2021 and 76.5% in FY2022 to $61.0 billion [F5][D161][F6][D200][F7][D238].
The FY2022 jump came from higher realized commodity prices and higher sales volumes, mostly from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59].
Revenue then fell 20.5% in FY2023 to $48.5 billion and has grown only 4.9% in FY2025 to $51.8 billion [F8][D274][F10][D342].
The FY2023 decline was driven by lower realized commodity prices across all products, partly offset by higher sales volumes [P47].
The U.S. supplied 79.1% of FY2025 revenue and added 5.7pp of the 4.9% growth [D382][D384][D342].
Crude oil was 66.3% of FY2025 revenue but grew only 0.1%, while natural gas grew 37.4% and contributed 4.4pp [D551][D552][D585][D586].
FY2025 revenue rose on higher volumes of $6,197 million, including Marathon Oil sales volumes, and higher realized gas prices of $824 million, partly offset by lower crude and bitumen prices [P28].
Net income fell 13.6% while revenue rose 4.9%, so there was no operating leverage in FY2025 [F20][D343][F10][D342].
Basic EPS fell 18.7%, faster than net income, because the diluted share count rose 6.1% [F40][D344][D356].
Net margin was 15.4% in FY2025, below its 17.9% window median and far under the 30.6% FY2022 high [F30][D831][D830].
Net margin fell 3.3pp in FY2025, after declines of 8.0pp in FY2023 and 3.9pp in FY2024 [D351][D283][D317].
DD&A rose $1,901 million in FY2025 on the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production volumes [P22].
Production and operating expenses rose $1,580 million, including $216 million of restructuring severance [P24].
The 36.9% effective tax rate exceeded the 32.4% of FY2024, widening the gap between pre-tax and net income [D332][D298].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, above the 1.52x of FY2022 [F59][F20][D333][D226].
Operating cash flow fell slightly in FY2025 on lower commodity prices, mostly offset by operations from the Marathon Oil acquisition [P6].
Operating cash flow was 33.6% of revenue in FY2025, against a 36.1% peak in FY2022 [D331][D224].
D&A reached 19.5% of revenue in FY2025, up from 9.6% in FY2022, while capex was 12.9% of revenue in FY2022 [D330][D221][D222].
Net cash was $7.1 billion, or 12.1% of revenue, in the 100th percentile of six energy peers against a -7.7% peer median [D337][D338][D850][D851].
Cash and investments rose 13.4% to $8.1 billion while total debt fell 1.4% to $1.0 billion [D335][D357][D336][D358].

FY2025 uses of cash were $12.6 billion of capex and investments, $5.0 billion of buybacks, $4.0 billion of dividends and $0.9 billion of debt retirement, partly offset by $3.2 billion of asset sales [P7].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.0 billion were 46% of operating cash flow, above the greater-than-30% framework [D339][F59][P31].
The revenue series mixes presentations: FY2025 is $51.8 billion in the table versus $58.9 billion as first reported [F10][X10].
Growth and margin comparisons across the window therefore mix a recast basis with originally reported years and should be read with care [R1].
Revenue fell 20.5% in FY2023 to $48.5 billion, the one clear down year outside the FY2020 collapse [F8][D274].
That decline came from lower realized commodity prices, partly offset by higher sales volumes [P47].
Segment revenue members sum to 227% of consolidated revenue in FY2025, so they cannot be added [R4].
Net margin: a print below the 17.9% window median would extend the three-year slide from the 30.6% FY2022 high [D831][D830][F30].
Operating cash flow: a move below the $19.8 billion FY2025 level would confirm the commodity-price drag the filing cites [F59][P6].
Net cash: a fall below the $7.1 billion FY2025 level would signal the buyback and capex programme outrunning cash generation [D337][P7].
